events.description: Husam Abd-al-Ra'uf killed in an Afghan NDS raid in Andar district, Ghazni; Christopher Miller later confirmed it and called it a major setback for al-Qaeda.
US-Taliban deal signed in Doha, pitched with Taliban counterterrorism assurances.
Op-ed by Christopher Miller calling Zawahiri al-Qaeda's sole ideological leader, which the hosts criticize.
Abdullah Azzam killed under mysterious circumstances; bin Laden folds Maktab al-Khidmat into al-Qaeda.
Vanguards of Khorasan launched with Raouf as editor; inaugural issue praised the 7/7 London bombings.
Taliban's As-Samud serialized Raouf's 'Victory of Islam' study across issues 2-6.
Vanguards of Khorasan interview with Raouf praising 9/11.
al-Qaeda reintroduced Raouf on video.
Aafia Siddiqui captured in Ghazni province.
Asim Umar, first AQIS emir, killed in a Taliban stronghold; no public acknowledgement.
Per the UN Monitoring Team report, an al-Qaeda delegation including Raouf, Ahmed al-Qatari, Sheikh Abdul Rahman and Abu Osman met Taliban over the Doha deal.
ISIS Yemen province video attacked al-Qaeda ideologically, singling out Raouf.
Taliban offensive in Lashkar Gah, prompting US airstrikes.
Taliban attacked an ANA base in Nimroz, killing 24 soldiers and capturing six.
Taliban killed 47 policemen, including the deputy provincial police chief, and captured six in a Taliban-controlled district of Takhar.
US airstrike in Wardak killed five Taliban fighters.
At least two US strikes in Idlib, Syria; targets unidentified, with one possibly Abu Muhammad al-Sadani.
Two recent US strikes in Idlib against al-Qaeda. Reported death tolls were inconsistent (10 or 17), and CENTCOM gave little information.
US-Taliban Doha deal, which the hosts argue should be nullified.
US presidential election, about one week after recording.
Planned recording of an episode with Lt. Gen. H.R. McMaster.

key_claims: Al-Qaeda has a significant network in Ghazni; Raouf could not have been based in Andar, a Taliban-controlled district, without it.
Raouf was a core al-Qaeda figure, not a local operative: he headed As-Sahab and edited Vanguards of Khorasan, and he was a founding-generation member who started at Maktab al-Khidmat.
The Taliban published Raouf's work in As-Samud, showing a long-standing al-Qaeda-Taliban link.
A 2020 UN Monitoring Team report said Raouf and other al-Qaeda leaders met the Taliban over the Doha deal.
The US government's claim of a single remaining al-Qaeda ideological leader contradicts its celebration of Raouf's killing.
No evidence shows the Taliban has broken with al-Qaeda; the hosts say the alliance is intact and the Taliban is gaining territory.
Al-Qaeda has not publicly acknowledged deaths such as Asim Umar's and probably will not acknowledge Raouf's until US forces leave.
The Taliban has escalated violence during the Doha talks, and the hosts say the Doha agreement contains no reduction-in-violence requirement.
The Khorasan Group was part of al-Qaeda, composed of al-Qaeda veterans, and was separate from the Nusra Front.
US strikes on the Khorasan Group were too few and too far between, leaving mid- and low-level cadres active and linked into al-Qaeda's network.
The hierarchy of al-Qaeda in Syria is muddled, and the US government has not explained it or its targeting choices.
Poor US transparency about strikes feeds the 'endless war' narrative.
The Taliban never held up their end of the Doha deal and have not broken with al-Qaeda, so the deal should be nullified.
A Biden plan to keep a small counterterrorism force in Afghanistan would likely require nullifying the Doha deal.
